issue.title: feat(mintd): allow multiple lightning backends per currency unit
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds support for running multiple Lightning backends in a single `cdk-mintd`, with each backend serving a different currency unit. So one mint can hand out sat-denominated ecash via CLN and eur-denominated ecash via LNbits, all through the same mint URL.

The mint engine itself already supported this (its payment-processor map is keyed by `(unit, method)`); the only thing blocking it was `cdk-mintd`'s config and startup, which assumed a single backend. This PR removes that assumption.

Closes #1465

## What operators see

Existing configs keep working. The old single `[ln]` block is still accepted and behaves identically to today.

For a multi-backend setup, repeat `[[ln]]` instead, one entry per `(unit, method)`:

```toml
[[ln]]
ln_backend = "cln"
unit = "sat"

[[ln]]
ln_backend = "lnbits"
unit = "eur"

[cln]
rpc_path = "..."

[lnbits]
admin_api_key = "..."
# ...
```

Each entry has its own mint/melt limits. Two entries pointing to the same `(unit, method)` are rejected at startup with a clear error.

### Description

This PR depends on #1797 

Add React Native bindings for the CDK wallet, following the same architecture as the existing Swift and Dart bindings. Uses uniffi-bindgen-react-native (v0.30.0-1) to generate TypeScript and C++ turbo module bindings from the shared cdk-ffi crate.

- bindings/react-native/rust/ — thin wrapper crate re-exporting cdk-ffi
- bindings/react-native/src/ — TypeScript entry point and turbo module spec
- bindings/react-native/cpp/ — generated C++ JSI bridge
- bindings/react-native/ios/ — iOS turbo module (Obj-C++)
- generate-bindings.sh — builds iOS/Android native libs and TS bindings

Tests mirror the Dart/Swift test cases by validating the generated TypeScript API surface: Wallet constructor, totalBalance, mintQuote, mint, generateMnemonic, sqliteWalletStore, and all associated types (Amount, WalletConfig, MintQuote, CurrencyUnit, PaymentMethod, SplitTarget).

Also updates the Nix flake to include Android SDK/NDK (27.0.12077973), cargo-ndk, and Node.js in the bindings devShell, and adds Android cross-compilation targets to the stable Rust toolchain.

Since this workflow calls all three via reusable workflow syntax, `swift-publish.yml` should also expose `workflow_call` with the same inputs. Right now Dart/Kotlin support `workflow_call`, but Swift only has `workflow_dispatch`, so the unified workflow will fail when it reaches Swift.
